Munajat-e-Maqbool

Thursday

Sixth manzil · supplications 175 to 190

Opening praise

In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

We praise You, O best of those in whom hope is placed and most generous of those from whom anything is sought, for teaching us Munajat-e-Maqbool, which brings nearness to Allah, and the supplications of the Messenger. Send perfect blessings upon him for as long as the west and east winds blow, and branches spring from their roots. Then we ask You for what we are about to recite. Ours is to ask, and Yours is to grant acceptance.

How to read

Read this opening invocation before each daily portion. Begin on Saturday, read one portion each day in order, and complete the cycle on Friday.

Swipe right to left to turn the page

In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

Supplication175

The Quran in heart and life

O Allah, I ask You by Muhammad, Your Prophet; Ibrahim, Your close friend; Musa, Your confidant; and Isa, Your spirit and Your word; and by the revelation given to Musa, the Gospel of Isa, the Psalms of Dawud, and the Criterion revealed to Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; and by every revelation You have sent down, or any decree You have ordained, any petitioner You have given to, any poor person You have enriched, any rich person You have impoverished, or anyone astray whom You have guided.

I ask You by Your name which You placed upon the earth so that it became firm, upon the heavens so that they were raised, and upon the mountains so that they stood firm. I ask You by Your name through which Your Throne became established. I ask You by Your pure, purified name, sent down in Your Book from Your presence; and by Your name which You placed upon the day so that it became light, and upon the night so that it became dark; and by Your greatness, Your majesty and the light of Your countenance:

grant me the mighty Quran, mingle it with my flesh, my blood, my hearing and my sight, and make my body act according to it, through Your strength and power. There is no strength and no power except through You. O Allah, do not let us feel secure from Your hidden plan, nor make us forget Your remembrance. Do not remove Your covering from us, and do not make us among the heedless.

Original commentary 175

This supplication may be understood as an appeal through the Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace; Ibrahim, the close friend of Allah; Musa; and Isa, peace be upon them; and through the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms and the Noble Quran. The request is: O Allah, grant me the Noble Quran so that it permeates my blood, my ears and my eyes, and make my body act upon it. Let me see through the eyes of the Quran, hear through its ears, and think about the Quran, so that it fills my life at every level and in every way. The Noble Quran is an everlasting miracle of Allah. He has placed such strength and power within it that, if a person sincerely reflects upon its meanings, it becomes clear that this is not the speech of a human being. Nowhere does this speech show any sign of being under pressure or of weakness. In the eleventh part [correctly, Surah Hud 11:44, in juz 12], the divine command addresses the earth and sky in this manner: O earth, swallow the water; O sky, stop raining. Could any worldly power issue such a command? Speech with this strength and power can only be Allah's speech, not that of any human being.

Sources and notesThursday · Prayer p. 123 · Composite from a rejected report and a weak reported prayer

Abu al-Shaykh, al-Thawab, quoted in al-Suyuti's al-Laʾali al-Masnuʿah

Locator: al-Laʾali 2/299 (also cited 2/357 by edition). Component: Opening through the request that the Quran permeate the body, ending 'no power or strength except through You', with abridgment and variants. Al-Suyuti: transmitter ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Harun is a liar, and the chain is also muʿdal. This is a rejected attribution in a story about Abu Bakr retaining the Quran; not an authenticated Quran-memorisation formula.

Abu Tahir al-Silafi, Ahadith Muntakhabah min Ajzaʾ Abi Mansur al-Khujani 15

Locator: 15; pp.96–97. Component: Final 'do not make us feel secure from Your plan; do not make us forget Your remembrance; do not remove Your covering; do not make us heedless'. Al-ʿIraqi calls the related al-Daylami route weak (al-Mughni 1/321); this precise route has not been independently graded here. The Arabic passage matches. Al-Iraqi's assessment of the related al-Daylami transmission is quoted in Islamweb research 142745.

Quran 11:44

Locator: Hud 11:44; juz 12. Excerpt: The earth-and-sky command quoted in the original commentary. Quranic text; hadith grading not applicable. The source commentary says eleventh part, but this ayah is in the twelfth juz.

Neither the long opening nor its attached promises should be presented as authenticated Prophetic teaching. The closing prayer has a separate source. The commentary's quoted Quran passage is 11:44, in juz 12; its eleventh-part label is a source error.

Supplication176

Well-being and relief in helplessness

O Allah, I ask You to hasten Your granting of well-being, to avert Your affliction, and to let me depart from this world into Your mercy. O You who suffice in place of everyone, while no one can suffice in Your place; O only One for those who have no one; O support of those who have no support: all hope has ended except hope in You. Deliver me from the state I am in, and help me against what has befallen me, by the honour of Your noble countenance and by Muhammad's right upon You. Ameen.

Original commentary 176

This supplication pleads before Allah in these words: O my Lord, bring me quickly out of sorrow and suffering, grant me peace and well-being, and remove all my afflictions. It also contains words for those who are helpless and without support: all my hopes in the world have come to an end; I seek help from You alone. In whatever affliction I find myself, help me, by Your pure Being and through Your noble Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, for whom You have granted the right of intercession according to Your promise.

Sources and notesThursday · Prayer p. 126 · Composite of disputed, historical and very weak reported prayers

Ibn Hibban 922; al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 1917; al-Tabarani, al-Duʿa 1452

Locator: 922; 1917; 1452. Component: Opening request for swift well-being and departure to divine mercy; source asks patience in affliction instead of removal of affliction. Al-Hakim: sahih chain; Shuʿayb al-Arnaʾut: weak chain. Al-Hakim and Shuayb al-Arnaut give different assessments of this transmission. Inclusion in a collection titled Sahih does not resolve that disagreement.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya, al-Faraj baʿd al-Shiddah 58

Locator: 58; p.63. Component: 'You suffice for all... O One for one who has no one; hope is cut off except from You' in a shorter form. Not a Prophetic report; historical account with an unnamed narrator; authenticity not assessed. Attributed to a captive in the reign of Sulayman ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, not to the Prophet.

Al-Daylami via Ibn Hajar, Zahr al-Firdaws 317

Locator: 1/702–703, no.317; al-Firdaws 1282 in another edition. Variant: The full continuation from O You who suffice for everyone through by Your noble countenance and Muhammad's right, including O support of one who has no support. Editor al-Arabi al-Daiz al-Faryati: this chain is very weak, with Shaqiq unidentified in reliability and two transmitters not located. The report reads release me (fukkani), where the anthology says deliver me (najjini), and supplies the complete closing appeal.

The complete closing appeal is preserved in a very weak report. Its historical parallel does not establish a Prophetic attribution. The opening has a separate grading disagreement and an affliction-wording variant.

Supplication177

Protection and gratitude despite shortcomings

O Allah, guard me with Your eye that never sleeps, shelter me by Your might that cannot be assailed, and have mercy on me through Your power over me, so that I do not perish while You are my hope. How many blessings You have bestowed upon me for which my gratitude to You has been small; and how many trials You have tested me with in which my patience before You has been small. O You who did not deprive me when my gratitude for Your blessing was small; O You who did not abandon me when my patience under Your trial was small; O You who saw me committing sins and did not expose me.

Original commentary 177

Reflect upon the translation of this supplication. It asks Allah, glorious is His majesty: O Allah, protect me with Your eye that never sleeps and with Your power, which no one can withstand. O Allah, I am at fault: I could not fulfil the duty of thanking You for Your blessings, and I did not remain patient in trials. It pleads humbly: grant me peace and well-being. Among the supplications transmitted from the Prophet, this is a remarkable prayer: it acknowledges human weakness and teaches us to ask Allah to grant us well-being, relief and tranquillity quickly.

Supplication178

Unending favour and protection from oppressors

O Bestower of goodness that never ends; O Possessor of blessings that can never be counted: I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad. And through You I confront the enemies and the tyrants.

Sources and notesThursday · Prayer p. 128 · Excerpt from the same very weak report as 177–179

Zahr al-Firdaws 614; Ibn ʿAsakir, Tarikh Dimashq 18/86

Locator: 614; 18/86; al-Sakhawi, al-Qawl al-Badiʿ p.334. Variant: The connected group of supplications printed as 177–179, including the well-being and independence clauses. Supplication179

Faith, provision and enduring well-being

O Allah, make worldly means a help to me in my religion, and make piety a help to me for my Hereafter. Guard for me what I am absent from, and do not leave me to myself in what I am present for. O You whom sins cannot harm and whom forgiveness cannot diminish, grant me what does not diminish You, and forgive me what does not harm You.

You are the Bestower. I ask You for relief soon, gracious patience, abundant provision, and well-being free from every affliction. I ask You for complete well-being, lasting well-being, and gratitude for well-being. I ask You for independence from people. There is no strength and no power except through Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.

Original commentary 179

This supplication asks Allah to make worldly means a help in religious progress, and piety a means of salvation in the Hereafter. It also teaches this lesson: even if the whole world were immersed in sins, You would suffer no loss whatsoever; and if You forgave everyone, Your treasure would not decrease by even a mustard seed.

Sources and notesThursday · Prayer p. 128 · Excerpt with variant endings from the same very weak report as 177–179

Zahr al-Firdaws 614; Ibn ʿAsakir, Tarikh Dimashq 18/86

Locator: 614; 18/86; al-Sakhawi, al-Qawl al-Badiʿ p.334. Variant: The connected group of supplications printed as 177–179, including the well-being and independence clauses. Al-Sakhawi: chain very weak. The report preserves an alternate ending. A related account in al-Dhahabi's Siyar 6/266–267 attributes the words to Jafar al-Sadiq without attributing them to the Prophet.

The additional requests for complete and lasting well-being, gratitude and independence are explicitly recorded as an alternate ending by al-Sakhawi. A shorter familiar phrase does not authenticate the whole expanded prayer.

Supplication180

Integrity within and without

O Allah, make my inward state better than my outward appearance, and make my outward life righteous. O Allah, I ask You for the good things You grant people: wealth, family and children, without going astray or leading others astray.

Original commentary 180

This supplication asks for the rectification of both the inward and outward self, and teaches us to ask that our inward state be even better than our outward appearance. It also asks concerning wealth, children and family: O Allah, protect them all from misguidance, so that they neither go astray themselves nor lead others astray. Include your family in your supplications.

Sources and notesThursday · Prayer p. 130 · Weak hadith report

Jamiʿ al-Tirmidhi 3586

Variant: all; final grammatical form varies slightly. Al-Tirmidhi: gharib and its chain is not strong; Darussalam: daʿif. Al-Tirmidhi records the Arabic prayer together with his own qualification of the transmission.

Source is clear; its inclusion in al-Tirmidhi does not mean it was graded sound.

Supplication181

Acceptance and a tranquil soul

O Allah, make us among Your chosen servants, with radiant faces and limbs, received as an accepted delegation. O Allah, I ask You for a soul at peace with You, believing in the meeting with You, content with Your decree, and satisfied with Your gifts.

Original commentary 181

This supplication asks: O Allah, make our faces and limbs radiant and shining in the Hereafter. Grant us a soul that is at peace with You, certain of meeting You, and content with the sustenance You provide. It also asks: O Allah, may I be content with Your decisions, so that I may attain a tranquil soul and the state of contentment.

Supplication182

Lasting praise and steadiness

O Allah, to You belongs praise: praise lasting as long as You endure. To You belongs praise: praise eternal with Your eternity. To You belongs praise: praise that has no end except by Your will. To You belongs praise: praise whose speaker seeks only Your pleasure. To You belongs praise at every blink of an eye and every breath of every soul. O Allah, turn my heart towards Your religion, and guard us from behind by Your mercy. O Allah, keep me firm lest I stumble, and guide me lest I go astray.

Original commentary 182

This supplication offers endless praise to Allah, exalted is His glory. Alongside it comes this remarkable request: O Allah, turn my heart towards Yourself. Protect us by Your mercy. Grant steadfastness, keep us firm upon guidance, and save us from going astray. These words also occur: O Turner of hearts, keep my heart firm upon the religion.

Sources and notesThursday · Prayer p. 132 · Composite; weak praise report, a separately graded heart prayer, and a disconnected report

The sources preserve variants of this praise; they do not establish the entire composite.

Supplication183

Protection of the heart and inward sufficiency

O Allah, just as You stand between me and my heart, stand between me and Satan and his work. O Allah, provide for us from Your bounty, do not deprive us of Your gifts, and bless what You have provided for us. Place our wealth within our souls, and direct our longing towards what is with You.

Original commentary 183

This supplication asks Allah, exalted is His glory: O Allah, become a barrier between me and Satan, so that I may escape sins and remain constantly engaged in Your obedience and worship. It also asks: O Allah, do not deprive us of sustenance from Your bounty. Grant us blessed provision, and make our hearts such that our selfish desires fade away and we hasten with eagerness and longing towards Your reward.

O Allah, make me among those who trust in You and for whom You are sufficient; who seek Your guidance and whom You guide; and who seek Your help and whom You help.

Supplication185

A heart occupied with remembrance

O Allah, turn the thoughts of my heart towards fear of You and remembrance of You. Direct my concern and desire towards what You love and are pleased with. O Allah, whatever ease or hardship You test me with, keep me firmly attached to the way of truth and the law of Islam.

Supplication187

Strength for striving in God’s cause

O Allah, Cleaver of the dawn, Maker of the night for rest, and of the sun and moon for reckoning, strengthen me for striving in Your path.

Original commentary 187

This supplication asks for strength to strive in Allah's path. This is the hope and desire of every Muslim, and the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) prayed for it for himself. We too make this request. O Allah, grant all Muslims strength of faith and the ability to sacrifice everything in Your path.

Sources and notesThursday · Prayer p. 135 · Traced to al-Daylamī through al-ʿIrāqī; authenticity not assessed

Supplication188

Praise for God’s care and gifts

O Allah, to You belongs praise for Your trials and Your dealings with Your creation. To You belongs praise for Your trials and Your dealings with the members of our households. To You belongs praise for Your trials and Your dealings with our own selves in particular. To You belongs praise for guiding us, praise for honouring us, praise for concealing our faults, and praise for the Quran. To You belongs praise for family and wealth, and to You belongs praise for well-being. To You belongs praise until You are pleased, and to You belongs praise when You are pleased, O You who are worthy of being feared and who alone grant forgiveness.

Original commentary 188

This supplication teaches a remarkable lesson: in every state and circumstance, however many hardships and troubles a person faces, he should embody contentment with Allah's decree and praise Him. Whatever Allah, exalted is His glory, does in His servant's affairs, no word of complaint or grievance should pass the servant's lips. In every circumstance, he should praise Allah and bow his head in submission before His decree. This alone is well-being, goodness and benefit.

Supplication190

Protection from harmful company and distress

O Allah, I seek refuge in You from a deceitful intimate friend whose eyes watch me while his heart lies in wait to harm me. If he sees a good deed, he conceals it; and if he sees a bad deed, he spreads it. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from poverty and severe hardship. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from Iblis and his armies.

O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the temptation of women. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from Your turning Your face away from me on the Day of Resurrection. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from every deed that disgraces me, and I seek refuge in You from every companion who harms me, every hope that distracts me, every poverty that makes me forget, and every wealth that makes me transgress. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from death through worry, and I seek refuge in You from death through grief.

Original commentary 190

By teaching us to protect ourselves from the evil of people living in this world, this supplication shows us that the world is full of deceitful friends who are friends in name but harbour ill will in their hearts. They conceal good qualities and eagerly spread faults. By teaching us to seek refuge from such people, it instructs us to protect ourselves from the troubles of this world. Alongside this comes another remarkable prayer: O Allah, I seek Your refuge from the temptation of women. The trial associated with women began in history with the son of Adam (peace be upon him), and in the present age it is the greatest trial. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) pointed to it in these words: 'After me, the most dangerous trial for men will be women.' O Allah, protect us all from this trial and from all trials.

Sources and notesThursday · Prayer p. 137 · Composite of differently transmitted supplications; not one authenticated report

Al-Tabarani, al-Dua 1339

Locator: 1339; al-Albani, al-Silsilah al-Sahihah 3137. Variant: Opening prayer against a deceitful intimate friend who hides good deeds and spreads faults. Al-Albani: good chain. Muhammad Amr Abd al-Latif disputes the raising of this report to the Prophet; see the following source. The compilation excerpts the final request of a longer report; it changes singular eye to plural eyes and has small connective variants.

Hannād ibn al-Sarī, al-Zuhd 2/645

Component: The opening prayer against a deceitful friend who conceals good and publicizes faults. al-Albānī, Ḍaʿīf al-Jāmiʿ 1199: weak as a Prophetic report. The primary wording is Saʿīd al-Maqburī’s report of a prayer of Dāwūd, not a connected report from Muḥammad.

Muhammad Amr Abd al-Latif, Tabyid al-Sahifah

Locator: 1/36; research answer 310963. Component: The dispute over the opening prayer against the deceitful friend. Muhammad Amr Abd al-Latif: the apparent chain is good, but connecting and raising it is an error; the correct form is Sa'id's report of Dawud's prayer. This criticism of the report's Prophetic attribution differs from al-Albani's positive assessment.

al-Ṭabarānī, Musnad al-Shāmiyyīn 745; Abū Nuʿaym, Maʿrifat al-Ṣaḥābah 6012

Locator: 745 (1/423) / 6012. Variant: Refuge from poverty and displaying poverty (al-buʾs wa-l-tabāʾus). No complete grading established here; the printed chain contains an unnamed transmitter. The report says 'I seek refuge in Allah' rather than the compilation’s direct 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You'.

Ibn al-Sunnī, ʿAmal al-Yawm wa-l-Laylah 155

Locator: 155; also Zahr al-Firdaws 788. Component: Refuge from Iblīs and his forces. al-Albānī, Ḍaʿīf al-Jāmiʿ 1369: very weak. The reported setting is leaving the mosque. Its guarantee of protection is not established.

al-Kharāʾiṭī, Iʿtilāl al-Qulūb 200

Locator: 200 (1/103). Excerpt: Refuge from temptation through women. al-Albānī, Ḍaʿīf al-Jāmiʿ 1203: weak. The source also asks protection from the punishment of the grave, omitted here.

al-Ṭabarānī, al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr 7048

Locator: 7048; also al-Bazzār 4638. Component: Refuge from God turning His face away on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn al-Qaṭṭān, Bayān al-Wahm wa-l-Īhām 3/367: Khubayb and his father are unknown. The same sentence occurs in no. 159.

al-Bazzār 7449; Abū Yaʿlā 4352; al-Ṭabarānī, al-Duʿāʾ 657

Locator: 7449 / 4352 / 657. Variant: Five requests against disgraceful work, harmful companionship, distracting hope, forgetfulness through poverty and arrogance through wealth. al-Bazzār calls Bakr ibn Khunays not strong; Ibn Ḥajar, Natāʾij al-Afkār 2/313: gharīb. Sources have a companion who ruins me (yurdīnī); the compilation has one who hurts me (yuʾdhīnī).

Aḥmad 8667 (edition 8652); al-Nasāʾī, al-Sunan al-Kubrā 7863

Locator: 8667 (14/303) / 7863. Variant: Closing requests against death through anxiety and distress. al-Nasāʾī identifies Ibrāhīm ibn al-Faḍl in the chain as abandoned. Ahmad's report has that I die in distress or anxiety. A separate Bayhaqi report has death by collapse and distress; the anthology's hamm (anxiety) is a distinct reading from hadm (collapse).

Sahih al-Bukhari 5096

Parallel only: The commentary's quotation about the trial that women can present to men; not the wording of the supplication. Sahih al-Bukhari. This authentic report supports the quoted warning. It does not verify the commentary's separate historical assertion about Adam's son.

Al-Raghib al-Isfahani, Mufradat, entry bus

Locator: Root b-ʾ-s. Parallel only: Lexical clarification of al-bus wa-l-tabaus in the Arabic; not a hadith authentication. Lexical source; hadith grading not applicable. Al-Raghib explains tabaus as making oneself appear wretched. The Urdu gloss expresses this more broadly as hardship; the English follows that gloss.

Each component has its own provenance. The opening has a positive grading by al-Albani and a specific competing analysis by Muhammad Amr Abd al-Latif. The commentary quotes an authentic warning in Bukhari 5096, but its historical claim about Adam's son was not established here. The Arabic tabaus means putting on an appearance of misery; the Urdu gloss and English translation render this more generally as hardship.

ClosingDurood

O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet, and upon his family, and grant them peace in abundance.

Note from the Urdu edition

Recite Durood at the beginning and end of every manzil. This is a means for supplications to be accepted. (See page 64 of the original edition.)

Reference review

The source’s instruction is retained above. Praise and blessings before duʿā have support in Abu Dawud 1481; the weekly arrangement is the compiler’s. The specific eighty-year reward quoted with Monday’s Durood has not been established as sound. See general references G1 and G3.

General blessings upon the Prophet are supported by Qur’an 33:56. A general encouragement does not by itself establish a particular count, occasion or reward.
